**Best value: ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037 400W kit — about $731.** It pairs a 1,024Wh LiFePO₄ battery with a 1,800W inverter and a generous 400W of panels—twice the panel wattage many kits in this class include. The listing also reports a discount code, so check the final price at checkout. [See the kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit)

If you’d rather stick with a more familiar brand, consider:

- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic + 220W panel — about $699.** It has the same 1,024Wh capacity and 1,800W output, plus fast AC charging and UPS switching. [Deal details](https://www.techradar.com/pro/ecoflows-delta-3-solar-generator-bundle-gets-a-usd300-price-drop-at-amazon-with-the-portable-power-station-and-220w-solar-panel-built-for-camping-home-backup-and-emergencies)
- **Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 — about $699.** A 1,070Wh LiFePO₄ battery and 200W panel make it a solid camping or outage option. [Compare kit details](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included)

Prices can change. For the best recharge potential under $1,000, I’d pick the **ALLPOWERS kit**; for a familiar brand with useful backup features, the **EcoFlow** is appealing.
